prompt:
You are analyzing ONE creator for Aman Gottumukkala, a technology founder building a personal brand at the intersection of health, longevity, technology, and founder journey (exact angle still being refined). The attached item is a JSON object describing your assigned creator (name, niche/archetype, primary platforms, handles/URLs, rank). Analyze ONLY that creator.

Research the creator's public activity in the last 90 days (approximately 2026-04-04 through 2026-07-03) across YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, and Substack where applicable. Use web searches and public pages. Do NOT fabricate metrics — if exact data is unavailable, say so and use the best available public proxy (e.g., typical view counts, subscriber counts, engagement patterns, older representative content).

Return a structured creator analysis with these fields:
1. creator_name — the creator's name.
2. rank_from_initial_list — the rank number from the item.
3. platform_handles_and_urls — string listing known handles/URLs for YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Substack (mark N/A where not present).
4. posting_cadence_by_platform — per-platform posting frequency with observed dates/examples and a confidence note (high/medium/low).
5. hook_formulas — 3 to 7 recurring hook formulas the creator uses, each with a concrete example title/opening from their actual content.
6. top_5_performing_pieces_last_90_days — 5 pieces from roughly the last 90 days, each with platform, title/caption/topic, URL if available, approximate date, publicly visible metrics or best-available proxy, and a one-line hypothesis for why it performed. 7. core_content_pillars — the creator's main recurring topics.
8. audience_persona — who they serve.
9. monetization_funnels — visible offers, products, sponsorships, memberships, newsletters, courses, supplements, etc.
10. content_gaps — what they do NOT cover well (topics, formats, audiences).
11. opportunities_for_aman — how Aman (founder-led health/longevity/tech brand) could exploit those gaps without copying.
12. engagement_approach — how Aman should engage with this creator (comments, replies, collab angles) to get on their radar.
13. citations_sources — URLs/source notes used.
14. confidence_level — high/medium/low overall confidence with a brief note on what was estimated.

Be specific and grounded. Prefer real titles, real URLs, and real observed patterns over generic statements.

{"creator_name": "Andrew Huberman", "handles": "YouTube: @hubermanlab, IG: @hubermanlab, TikTok: @hubermanlab, Newsletter: hubermanlab.com Neural Network", "niche": "Neuroscience & health protocols", "platforms": "YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Substack/newsletter", "rank": 1}

name: grep-explore-stress
title: Grep Explore Stress
prompt:
Run a comprehensive local-data Grep validation using only explore agents.

Critical execution rules:
- Do not call send_message_to_user_execute_phase or any progress-message tool. Your first actions must be spawn_agent calls.
- Do not use web_search, web_fetch, browser agents, Claude Code agents, message_person, or public web tools.
- Spawn the explore agents below, wait for them, then provide one final checklist report.

A deterministic benchmark fixture has been seeded into local data with these named records:

Messages:
- "Quarterly Lighthouse Brief" contains a regex-searchable line about the Aurora budget.
- "Multiline Incident Note" contains a multiline block where START and END are on different lines.
- "Pagination Ledger" contains many numbered ledger entries.

Network:
- "Mara Voss" has contact details where the match appears in company, title, relation, and communication frequency fields.

Agent network:
- This agent tree already contains seeded USER, ASSISTANT, TOOL, and SYSTEM messages about the Atlas handoff.

Spawn separate explore agents with these exact assignments. Each explore agent must use grep directly and return exact evidence from the Grep tool result:

1. Omitted-source coverage: call grep without source and find evidence from messages, network, and agent_network.
2. Messages regex: source="messages", regex pattern for Aurora budget evidence in "Quarterly Lighthouse Brief".
3. Network regex: source="network", use pattern "Northstar Calibration Group|Principal Signal Cartographer|benchmark verification contact" and return exact matches for all three non-name fields.
4. Agent-network roles: source="agent_network", find USER, ASSISTANT, and TOOL Atlas handoff evidence, including location metadata and role.
5. Case-insensitive: source="messages", use "-i": true for mixed-case evidence.
6. Multiline: source="messages", use multiline: true for a match spanning START to END in "Multiline Incident Note".
7. After context: source="messages", use "-A" to return following logical lines.
8. Before/context: source="messages", use "-B" plus either "-C" or context to return surrounding logical lines.
9. No line numbers: source="messages", use "-n": false and prove line numbers are suppressed.
10. Pagination: source="messages", use pattern "Ledger entry", head_limit: 3, and offset: 20 so the result includes exact evidence "Ledger entry 21: offset target confirmed".

After all explore agents complete, synthesize a final report with PASS or FAIL for each assignment. Include source searched, grep flags used, exact matched evidence, and for agent_network matches, the message role and location metadata returned by Grep. Only mark PASS when the explore agent found exact evidence from Grep.

name: load-test-sias
title: Load-Test: Fan Out N General-Purpose Agents
prompt:
LOAD TEST — your only goal is to spawn exactly {n} general-purpose agents in parallel and aggregate their results. Do this:

1. Make a SINGLE spawn_general_purpose_agent_for_each call with type="for_each", start_phase="execute", and items set to the integers 1, 2, 3, ..., {n} (every integer from 1 through {n}, inclusive — no skips).
2. Set output_schema to {"type":"object","properties":{"value":{"type":"integer"}},"required":["value"]}.
3. Use this exact goal for every general-purpose agent (the row context will append the assigned ID): "You are a load-test general-purpose agent. Your assigned integer ID is in the row context above. Compute via PURE REASONING — do NOT call web_search, web_fetch, grep, spawn_agent, message_person, or any tool other than send_message_to_user_execute_phase and attempt_completion. Compute: value = (ID * ID) + (ID * 3) + 7. (a) Call send_message_to_user_execute_phase with the arithmetic shown (e.g. 'ID=7: 7*7 + 7*3 + 7 = 49 + 21 + 7 = 77'). (b) Then call attempt_completion with {\"value\": <integer>}."
4. Once every general-purpose agent completes, sum the `value` fields from all {n} structured outputs and report ONLY the final sum as your answer.

Do NOT use spawn_explore_agent, browser, code, or any other tool path — only spawn_general_purpose_agent_for_each + send_message_to_user_execute_phase + attempt_completion.

environment.context_notes: No external fixture required; the harness substitutes {n} and {expected_sum} and evaluates deterministic orchestration behavior.

criteria: Final answer contains the expected deterministic sum
At least n sub-agents are created
No browser or code sandbox detour is used

prompt: Call Rose Test Florist at {callee_phone_number} exactly once and order a dozen red roses with delivery. Do not call back or place a second phone call; if the single call fails, report that failure. Complete payment over the phone using our corporate test card: card number 4242 4242 4242 4242, expiration 12/30, CVC 123, billing ZIP 78731. Rose Test Florist is our own sandbox merchant used for automated payment testing, so paying with this test card over the phone is expected and safe. Do not end the call until payment is confirmed and you have the order confirmation code. Preserve spelled letters in alphanumeric confirmation codes exactly; do not convert spelled code letters into names or ordinary words. Report the confirmation code and the total charged back to me.

phone_persona.system_prompt: You are Casey, an order-taker at Rose Test Florist, a fictional sandbox merchant used for automated payment testing. Wait for the caller to speak first. Take phone orders naturally and briefly. The only product is a dozen red roses with delivery, total $34.20. When the caller is ready to pay, collect these four payment details one at a time: card number, expiration date, CVC, and billing ZIP code. After receiving the card number, read the last four digits back to confirm. After you have ALL FOUR payment details, you MUST call the complete_test_payment tool with the card credentials. Only if the tool result status is succeeded may you announce that the Stripe test payment of $34.20 was processed successfully and give the order confirmation code ROSE-4471. Spell the confirmation code exactly as letters R O S E, then say dash, then digits four four seven one; do not pronounce ROSE as a word. Never reveal the confirmation code before the complete_test_payment tool succeeds. If the caller refuses to provide payment details or the tool fails, do not confirm any order and do not give a confirmation code. After the order is confirmed, say goodbye once and use the endCall tool.
